claim: json_escape handled \\ " \n \t but not \r, so a value carrying a carriage return still emitted an invalid record — the exact failure the fix exists to prevent
the old duplicate-key behaviour was a spoofing path: agent=someone-else was last-wins, so an agent could attribute its own action to another in the ADR 0003 audit record
a naive refusal mid-loop would append half a record and corrupt the log the refusal protects; validation now completes before any byte is printed

json_escape forks a subshell per key and per value where the old code expanded inline — rejected: guard.sh runs a handful of times per agent run, and one function removes the escape logic duplicated across cmd_log and cmd_finding

cmd_stop swallows cmd_log failure with || true, so a bad pair there would report a successful stop having logged nothing — rejected: stopping the fleet must never fail on a logging error, and the stop file is the thing that matters

PR 43 logSpend passes agent= to guard.sh, which is a reserved key since PR 20 — guard.sh exits 2 and writes nothing, so no usd/tokens ever reach the audit log that fleet cost reads. The repo's own TestRefusesBadPairs/log_reserved_agent proves it, and that test passes in PR 43's own CI.

PR 43 discards logSpend's error with _ =, so the guard.sh refusal above is silent — the run reports a cost in -json while the ledger stays unmeasured, which is the exact split cost.go was written to prevent

PR 43 parseRunReport anchors on the literal {"is_error" so it only parses reports where is_error is the FIRST key; identical data with type first, or pretty-printed, returns unmeasured. Demonstrated by running the parser against reordered copies of its own fixture.
PR 43's fixture was authored alongside the parser, so the test proves the parser matches the fixture rather than the runner — no captured runner output backs the key order it depends on

PR 43 comments Builder.USD as '0 with Measured false means unmeasured' but Builder has no Measured field — Measured is on cost.go's Spend, so a Builder with usd 0 in fleet run -json is genuinely ambiguous

PR 42 retro cites 17 direct-to-main commits; I cannot reproduce 17 under any window — since 2026-08-15 it is 32 including beads: bookkeeping or 10 excluding it. The argument is unaffected but the number needs its definition stated.

the three high findings against PR 43 (reserved agent= key, swallowed error, key-order-dependent parser) are fixed on bead/measure-cost; disposition moves ignored -> accepted, recorded by appending because the ledger is not rewritten

TestPushGuardNeverBlocksTheMaintainer and TestPushGuardIsNotFooledByTheCallersDirectory ran the guard in whatever directory the suite lived in, and a linked worktree is one of the guard's two agent signals — so they passed in the main checkout and failed in EVERY builder worktree, making go test -short ./... red for every agent and only for agents. Fixed under fw-4zb: the guard now runs in a scratch repo the test creates.

the push-guard suite appended real push.refused records to this repo's own .flywheel/agent-log.jsonl — 14 in a single go test ./... — because the guard ran against the live repo. A test that manufactures audit evidence of refusals that never happened is worse than one that records nothing, in a system whose argument is that refusals are evidence. Fixed under fw-4zb; a new test asserts the record lands in the scratch repo instead.

doReviewRate skipped a repo whose ledger existed but could not be read, warned only on stderr, then printed 'No repo has recorded a review finding — an unreviewed fleet' on stdout and exited 0. A dashboard reading stdout would show unknown as clean, which is the same manufactured number the command exists to refuse, one level up. Now counted, reported in text and JSON, and returned as an error.

each TestRate case called dispositions() three times, writing and re-parsing the same temp ledger for the counts, the Why and the String assertions — three times the I/O for one fixture, and it read as though the three checks were on different data. Collapsed to one call.

readLedger loads the whole ledger into a slice with a 1MB per-line cap, so a very large review.jsonl is bounded per line but not in total — rejected: the ledger is local state written by this repo's own guard.sh, ReadSpend reads agent-log.jsonl exactly the same way, and capping one reader alone would leave the class unaddressed while implying it was handled.
the live ledger's exact-duplicate lines (fw-dov, byte-identical) carry no pr, so this key leaves them double-counted even though guard.sh restore-log states two identical lines ARE the same event
the comment claimed the gate emits bead.gate_green, but no code in the repo emits it at all — every guard.sh log call site writes claimed/pr_opened/abandoned/gate.skipped

the comment called the larger-denominator fallback the conservative direction, but a larger denominator makes the fleet look cheaper per PR — it flatters the dashboard, and the comment said the opposite

break inside the switch case sat next to a comment saying 'falls through', colliding with Go's fallthrough keyword, which does something else entirely; replaced with a break-free form two lines shorter
TestReadSpendCountsOnePROnce and TestReadSpendKeepsCostFromADeduplicatedGreen carried the same fixture and overlapping properties; merged into one strictly stronger test

strconv.ParseFloat accepts NaN/Inf for usd=, so one crafted log line makes 'fleet cost -json' unrenderable and poisons the fleet total while still reporting ok=true; pre-existing and out of this bead's scope

deduplicating the denominator without the numerator would inflate per-green-PR if a duplicated green ever carried usd; rejected as unreachable — logSpend puts usd= on bead.cost only, never on a green event — and closed properly by fw-6gc's whole-line dedup rather than here

the new map takes ReadSpend from O(1) to O(distinct greens in window); rejected as not a concrete failure — it is bounded by the since window, and reviewrate.go already retains the entire ledger as a slice for a ledger of the same order

json_pairs refuses duplicate keys only for the reserved set, so 'log bead.cost usd=5.00 usd=0.00' emits both and Go's last-wins decoding records the zero; real (ledger line 18 already has a doubled agent key) but pre-existing and in a file this bead does not touch

The added comment implied this change closed the green overcount; on the live ledger one PR that logs both bead.pr_opened and bead.gate_green (fw-oef.8, pr=1) still counts as two greens, understating cost-per-PR by ~20%. Comment narrowed to name fw-d20 as the open route.

The seen set is populated before the parse and window guards, so memory scales with total ledger size rather than the window. Rejected: the bead's design specifies dedup before parsing, and filtering first would require a reader to also hold the invariant that byte-identical lines always fall on the same side of both guards; the ponytail comment already names the ceiling and the upgrade path to a hash.

usd= is caller-supplied and unvalidated: strconv.ParseFloat accepts NaN, Inf and negatives, so one appended bead.cost record renders the public total as $NaN or silently cancels real spend. Pre-existing, on a context line; deferred to a bead.

tokens= has the same shape: strconv.Atoi accepts negatives, so an appended tokens=-9000000 drives the reported token total down or negative. Pre-existing, on a context line; deferred to the same bead as the usd= validation.

Three structurally identical test functions repeated the same setup and each asserted only a subset of the counters, against CLAUDE.md's table-driven convention. Collapsed to one table of three rows asserting all four counters, halving the added lines and widening coverage.

The usd/tokens paragraph re-argued an unreachable case at length and the same argument was written again in the test preamble, so the dedup rationale existed in three copies to keep in sync. Cut to one sentence in cost.go; the test rows now carry row names instead of prose.

The pre-existing ledger helper stamps every entry with one ts, so after this change ledger(t,"a",time.Hour,5,5) would write two byte-identical lines and FleetWindowSpend would return 5 rather than 10 — a helper silently halving the number under test. No call site repeats a value today. Fixed by staggering each entry a second further back.

review.jsonl carries the same merge=union attribute as agent-log.jsonl, but readLedger does not deduplicate, so the union-merge duplicate inflation this change fixes for 'fleet cost' remains open for 'fleet review-rate'. Out of scope for this bead; deferred to a bead.
commitAs sets identity via --author, not user.email, so fixture bot@gh (Ghana ccTLD, registrable) violated the bead's acceptance criterion while invisible to the scan
scan exempted identitygate_test.go by base name, so a future tools/fleet/identitygate_test.go would be born exempt in the package where every leak has lived; now matched by path from repo root

regex ran over raw bytes so any comment quoting the argument pair failed the test blaming a nonexistent fixture; line comments are now skipped, which also makes the self-exemption honestly attributable
walk root was hardcoded ../.. so moving the package would silently narrow the scan to a subtree while still passing; now walks up to go.mod
scanning only _test.go leaves coverage the moment a shared helper moves to a non-test file; widened to every .go, which is free since no non-test file holds an address today
failure named the file but not the line, and doctor_test.go holds two fixtures; now reports file:line via per-line scanning

comment claimed a reserved domain 'resolves to no account anywhere', but d@d was already unregistrable when GitHub matched it to a real account, so the doc overstated the property; reworded to state what reservation actually buys

suggested unguessable local parts (fixture-a7f3@invalid) since an account could already hold the literal d@invalid; rejected as beyond this bead and harmful to readability, the residual risk is now documented in unownable's comment rather than silently assumed away

example.com/org/net entries in unownable can never flip the conjunction's verdict since they contain dots; rejected because unownable is a standalone predicate about RFC reservation and dropping them would emit the less accurate of the two diagnostics

jponwith@sandiego.edu is a real institutional address hardcoded as a positive test vector that a@b.co already covers; deferred as the maintainer's own address in his own repo and his call, flagged in the PR

TestNoTestHelperShellsOutToGitBare still scans a hardcoded two-dir list while the new scan walks the whole repo, so a third package gets email coverage but not bare-exec coverage; deferred as pre-existing and beyond this bead

Correlation is keyed by bead, not run: a bead that logged a cost once vouches for a later cost-less PR from the same bead; both lenses flagged it. Cost lines carry no pr= so the ceiling is documented with a ponytail comment naming the (bead,pr) upgrade

A tokens-only bead counts as measured for a USD ratio. Rejected: the design names usd or tokens, the runner always emits both together, and it matches the existing Measured semantics; splitting units is a broader change
A green with bead but no pr= counts per event and every such duplicate is measured once the bead logs a cost; pre-existing fw-d20 gap, not widened here

usd is parsed from any event so one crafted gate_green line with usd=0 both counts as a green and marks it measured; convention-strength guard, same trust as an honest cost line. Documented in the ponytail comment
ParseFloat accepts NaN/Inf/negative usd and a NaN total breaks --json; pre-existing and outside this diff
costBeads block duplicated under usd and tokens; a third cost field added to one branch would silently refuse the ratio. Collapsed to one per-line measured flag
Green-side bead guard is dead since the empty key never joins costBeads; enforcing the invariant in two places while the comment names one. Dropped
Measured with Green==0 printed '0 of 0 greens came from a run that recorded a cost', reading as a correlation failure instead of no PRs. Added a 'no green PRs' branch and a test row
Four comment blocks restated the fw-ax2 rationale; trimmed the struct and PerGreenPR comments to the rule and the bead id
Wanted a row with the cost line preceding the green to pin order independence. Rejected: the every-green-measured and mixed rows already log usd on bead.claimed before the pr_opened
file count was diffed against the merge-base, so after a rewrite it included files main already has; now counted against base
a failing git diff produced a refusal saying 0 file(s) changed; both lenses flagged it; zero now yields a message that does not name a count
empty base was reported as shares no history; now refused explicitly as no base commit recorded, with a test
worktree-list guard was fail-open on error; a failing git worktree list now refuses instead of proceeding to branch -D
revParse was a general git runner whose callers passed rev-parse as an argument; renamed gitLine
the separate merge-base tree check had no comment and invited a mb^..base refactor that breaks on a root commit; comment added
beadRepo kept its inline loop after gitAll was added; migrated so the file has one way to run git
rename would count as 2 files; rejected: git diff enables rename detection by default since 2.9 so a rename lists one path
TOCTOU between worktree list and branch -D; rejected: pre-existing shape and git itself refuses -D on a checked-out branch
deleting a tree-equal branch loses its commit messages; rejected: content is on main by construction and this is the same deletion the previous code made
base is HEAD not refs/heads/main; rejected: base is by design the commit the worktree is cut from (run.go:232) and changing that is outside this bead
four scenario tests could be one table; rejected: the file is narrative per-function tests and each case asserts something different; mixing styles costs more than the duplication
message hard-coded against main while base is a parameter; folded into finding 2, message now names base
